applied.problem: The practice states two conventions as absolute rules Dan will act on: on older sheets using the hump convention a plain crossing can be a joint, and contacts are only usually drawn coil-off (the explanation itself hedges this with "textbooks add").

"Each part carries one name on the plant and on the drawing" is stated as fact though plant labels can be missing or wrong (the practice says to check them); and the lamp stays lit when the motor stops only while the isolator is closed.
It names the hump convention but not its consequence: on such sheets a plain crossing with no hump can mean the lines are joined, the opposite of the no-dot rule taught here.
